_comment: JINGLE FORMS AND CHARACTERS. A jingle is not a genre and not a loop: it is a SHORT THROUGH-COMPOSED piece with a beginning, a hook, and an ending it stops on. Its identity comes from FUNCTION, CHARACTER and PRODUCTION — not from a genre. READ LOOPSTAR_SOUL.md BEFORE EDITING: the palette is the app's own synth voices (1000+) and 808/synth kits, never GM brass, winds, bowed strings or novelty instruments. Character comes from production — sub weight, filter movement, space — not from a literal instrument standing in for a subject.

forms.name: Button
forms.blurb: The full stop. One accent, held, then silence. What ends a segment.

forms.name: Sting
forms.blurb: One gesture and a stop. Scene transitions, reveals, punchlines.

forms.name: Logo
forms.blurb: An identity motif — three to five notes you could hum back. Sparse; the notes carry it, not the groove.

forms.name: Bumper
forms.blurb: In and out of a break. States the hook once, answers it, stops.

forms.name: Theme
forms.blurb: A show's front title: sets up, states the hook, answers it, lifts, lands.

_sectionRoles.intro: Sets the key and the pulse. Thinner than the hook — it is a runway.
_sectionRoles.gesture: A single rising or falling figure. The whole point of a sting.
_sectionRoles.motif: The identity cell: 3-5 notes with one leap. Repeatable, hummable, no groove needed.
_sectionRoles.hook: The memorable phrase. Densest melodic writing; everything else supports it.
_sectionRoles.answer: The hook's reply — same rhythm, different contour, or the same contour a step away.
_sectionRoles.lift: One bar of rising tension into the button. Often a fill or a held dominant.
_sectionRoles.button: The ending. An accent on beat 1, held and allowed to ring. NOTHING after it.

characters.name: Signal
characters.blurb: Authority through sub weight and space, not brass. A rising saw stab over a hard kick.

characters.name: Playful
characters.blurb: Bright plucks and pitch-bent 808s. Light and fast without a xylophone in sight.

characters.name: Absurd
characters.blurb: A sound that arrives wrong. Detuned, off-grid, filtered somewhere unexpected — a modifier that colours whatever it meets.

characters.name: Clean
characters.blurb: Resolved and unhurried. A wide pad, a crystalline bell, nothing that surprises.

characters.name: Impact
characters.blurb: Hard 808 kick and a wide supersaw stab. Built for a room.

characters.name: Retro
characters.blurb: Square and saw leads, bone dry. Arcade without the twee.

characters.name: Noir
characters.blurb: A detuned pad and a filtered sub that never quite resolves. No tremolo strings.

characters.name: Warm
characters.blurb: A soft pad and an electric-piano figure. Unhurried, no acoustic guitar.

_defaults.note: A brief matching no character still gets a real jingle. 'clean' is the least-wrong neutral and is modern-electronic like everything else — there is no orchestral fallback, by design.

_fxComment: Per-character MIX. gain is linear, pan is -1..1, reverb and delay are 0..1 wet. delayNote is a TEMPO-SYNCED division (1/4, 1/8, 1/8d, 1/8t, 1/16) resolved against the piece's BPM at render time — a delay in seconds lands on nothing and is the clearest tell of a preset. lead/pad/drums are the three layers.

soul._comment: The sound identity, machine-readable. Prose lives in LOOPSTAR_SOUL.md; this is the part a planner has to obey. `avoidPrograms` are GM ranges that make LoopStar sound like a 50s game show — fake brass, thin winds, low-resolution bowed strings, clean guitars, novelty. A model asking for one of these gets `substitute` instead, chosen so the GESTURE survives and only the timbre changes.

avoidPrograms.why: clean/acoustic guitars — thin and fake at GM resolution
bowed strings — low-resolution sample, immediately corny
winds and reeds — nasal, never edgy
novelty and world — banjo, bagpipe, steel drum, whistle

soul._substituteComment: Fallback lead when a banned program is requested — an app synth voice (programs 1000+ route to LoopStarSynthEngine). Change this id to re-point every rejection at once, no rebuild.
